content.title: About
content.content: Dessert pizza is a sweet pastry, usually with a thin crust, topped with cream, fruit, berries, chocolate or nuts. It combines the crunchy base of a traditional pizza with a variety of dessert toppings, making it a popular treat for parties and family meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first dessert pizza was served in Italy in the 1970s as an experimental twist on classic pizza.
There are many variations: berry sauce, caramel, Nutella, ricotta cheese, and even ice‑cream topped versions.
Dessert pizza is often presented as a "pizza‑cake" with multiple layers of dough alternating with cream and fruit.
In Japan, a popular "mochi pizza" replaces the dough with a sweet rice cake base, topped with fruit and sweet paste.
Sweet pizza is believed to keep children more engaged than a regular dessert because of its interactive presentation.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The crust and sweet toppings provide carbohydrates that quickly replenish glycogen stores.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Fruits and berries used as toppings are rich in vitamin C, potassium and antioxidants.

items.title: Calcium from ricotta
items.content: Ricotta or mascarpone, commonly used in dessert pizzas, are good sources of calcium.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Sweet flavors stimulate serotonin production, helping to lift mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Toppings often contain nuts, dairy or gluten, which may trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The crust and creamy toppings make dessert pizza calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve dessert pizza warm or at room temperature. Cut into serving slices, add fresh berries, dust with powdered sugar or drizzle with chocolate sauce. It pairs well with ice cream or whipped cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the finished pizza in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in the oven for 5‑7 minutes before serving to restore a crisp crust. Frozen pizza can be stored for up to 1 month, wrapped tightly in plastic film and foil.
